points.text: No related-work section; new versus known contributions not separated.
Practical claim rests on one small CIFAR-10 FID experiment without variance.
Sections 5.2-5.3 supported by single image sets only.
'Without Markov chains and SDEs' overclaims; coefficients derived from Markov-chain posterior.
Claim contradicting prior understanding not substantiated by testing trained models.
Typos and cross-reference errors.
Prior work on linear-combination samplers, solver search and unified solvers uncited; C2/C3 not novel.
Degradation finding restates known empirical-denoiser memorization; memorization literature uncited.
Empirical-posterior statistics do not support conclusions about what trained networks learn.
Self Guidance explanation ignores standard accounts of CFG failure and multistep extrapolation weights.
Exposure-bias literature missing for over-enhancement section.
Generic hyperparameter-optimization survey cited instead of diffusion-solver search work.
Leap from posterior collapse to models failing to learn ignores generalization; no trained-model test.
Abstract states collapse generally, but none occurs at high noise.
Whether posterior is conditional or unconditional is unstated.
'Without Markov chains and SDEs' overclaims given Markov-chain derived coefficients.
Unification is numeric, approximate and only for linear samplers.
Table 3 evidence: one dataset, one model, single run.
Coefficient search unstated and with larger search space than baselines.
No UniPC or learned-solver baselines.
Self Guidance mechanism inferred from sign patterns and one image set; confounded.
Training-testing consistency claim contradicts stated train-test mismatch.
Optimized matrices with negative weights not tested under CFG.
'Inversely proportional to distance' misdescribes Eq. 22 weights.
Numerical counts (10 million, 16,480) incorrect.
Notation problems: X1 for xt, ε treated as constant, wrong distribution label.
Wording and cross-reference errors such as 'higher FID' and 'Table 3.2'.
Missing connections to kernel regression, statistical physics, multistep methods and Wiener filtering.
Optimized matrices are specific to model, step count and time grid.
Not evaluated with guidance or on text-to-image models where negative weights should fail.
Finite-training-set posterior assumed though trained networks generalize beyond it.
Training-testing consistency assumed despite identified mismatch.
CIFAR-10 FID assumed to represent quality at scale.
Broader impact on memorization, privacy, copyright not discussed.
Coefficient optimization procedure undocumented; search space asymmetric versus baselines.
FID details and seeds unstated; single run cannot separate small margins from noise.
Explanatory claims correlational, rest on single qualitative examples; no interventions.
Unification holds by construction for linear samplers, approximate, error unquantified.
Table 1/2 protocol under-specified: time unit, conditioning, latent scaling, schedule.
No experiment relating posterior statistics to trained network outputs.
Weight description of Eq. 22-23 wrong.
Flow-matching derivation wrongly treats ε as constant under the posterior integral.
Two dataset statistics do not add up.
Typos, cross-reference and notation errors.
Language vague and analysis not rigorous.
Claim that models cannot learn posterior/score lacks rigorous argument; ignores convergence theory.
Weighted sum degradation is expected, not original.
Unified inference section only reinterprets existing methods; no new insights or methods.
Claim about learning in high-dimensional sparse settings lacks references or evidence.
Equation 15 unclear since expectation taken over xt rather than x0.
Figure 1 appears incorrect.
Lack of experiments in main text.
No related work section.
Redundant content, including proofs of well-known equivalences.
Formatting issues: excessive emphasis, caption periods, 'Eq. equation'.
Figure 5 cluttered with unexplained symbols.
Main claim overstated: posterior concentration does not invalidate probabilistic formulation.
Natural Inference Framework only re-expresses known samplers; no new theory or algorithm.
No experimental evidence that perspective improves understanding or performance.
False 'first rigorous analysis' claim; existing literature not cited or compared.
Appendix proofs are known results not acknowledged as such.
Section 2 diffusion/flow-matching similarity is well known and uncited.
Many statements vague or undefined; Section 4.1 lacks rigor.
No real contribution presented.
Self guidance and natural inference not concretely defined; Section 4.2 unclear.
No empirical results comparing new framework with known samplers.
Appendix proofs imprecise: f_theta undefined, missing norms.
Flow matching discussion incorrect in general; only Gaussian-prior special case.
Flow matching statistics differ due to noise schedule, not explained.
Degradation is not equivalent to single-sample estimation; single samples work for VAEs.
Learning the ideal target is undesirable since it cannot generate unseen data.
Figure 5 difficult to parse with undefined symbols.
Self guidance resembles uncited Autoguidance.

P.summary: No related work; new vs known unclear.
Prior solver-search and unified-solver work uncited.
Degradation restates known memorization; literature uncited.
Missing connections to neighboring-field results.
Posterior statistics do not show trained models fail to learn; generalization ignored.
Collapse claim overgeneral; absent at high noise.
Tables 1-2 protocol under-specified.
'Without Markov chains/SDEs' overclaim.
Unification approximate, by construction, linear samplers only.
Quantitative evidence limited to one small dataset/model.
Coefficient search undocumented and asymmetric vs baselines.
Single run; FID details unstated; margins within noise.
Missing UniPC/learned-solver baselines.
Mechanism claims correlational, based on single qualitative examples.
Standard explanations of CFG/high-order behavior not discussed.
Exposure-bias literature missing.
Train-test consistency claim contradicts mismatch.
Optimized matrices untested under guidance/text-to-image.
Optimized matrices specific to model and step grid.
Broader impact not discussed.
Kernel weight description wrong.
Dataset count errors.
Flow-matching derivation treats ε as constant; notation errors.
Typos and cross-reference errors.
Inappropriate citation for coefficient search.

Q.summary: Main claim that models cannot learn distribution is unsupported/overstated.
Inference framework only re-expresses known samplers; no contribution.
No related work; false 'first' claim; literature ignored.
Known results presented without attribution; redundancy.
Flow-matching statistics difference misattributed; noise schedule.
Degradation not equivalent to single-sample estimator.
Learning ideal target undesirable; generalization question.
